_: Verified Romanian shop lines, carried over from the catalog this one replaces.
These 256 rows are the one thing worth keeping from the previous catalog: they
were curated by hand, they are real products from real Romanian shelves, and
their weights below are not invented -- each one is what the row had actually
earned from people adding it to real shopping lists before that project was
wiped. Nothing else survived, and nothing here was reconstructed from memory.
WHY THEY ARE ROMANIAN-ONLY AND STAY THAT WAY. Every name is the name printed
on the pack in Romania. Translating "Chipsuri cu Smantana si Verdeturi 140g"
into five languages would invent five commercial facts (S4: never invent
commercial facts), and the pack in Germany is a different pack with a
different name. So these carry lang=ro, markets=[RO], and no aliases. A German
household will not see them ranked highly, which is correct -- they cannot buy
them.
WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY DROPPED. The old rows had no category and no barcode for
253 of the 256, and neither was reconstructed: a guessed category is a wrong
search result and a guessed barcode is a wrong product. They stay blank until
Open Food Facts or an admin fills them in, which the importer permits (blanks
may always be filled).
The weight is capped at 100 so the seed keeps one editorial scale: 100 is a
weekly staple in generics.json too, and a row that had earned 131 taps in a
catalog that no longer exists should not start above every staple in this one.
type is generic where the row has no brand -- "Rosii 1kg" is a shop line, not
a manufactured product, and the quality rules for a generic (no barcode needed,
no brand needed) are the right ones for it.
